title: Headlines
verdict: Export engine cools — RMG to EU down 16.4%, exporters seek bill relief.
tldr: RMG's EU slump and exporter energy stress lead a credit-cycle tape.
analysis: Today's tape runs on a single thread: the credit cycle is turning where Bangladesh earns its dollars. RMG exports to the EU, the largest apparel market, fell 16.4% in H1, and exporters are asking to spread July-August utility bills over twelve months — working-capital stress at the export coalface that lands on back-to-back LC lines before it reaches a quarterly NPL print. That strain meets a book with no give: private credit dead at a 33-year-low 4.98%, NPLs 32.26% on the Q1 read, the capital cushion already gone. Easing gas supply and Adamjee EPZ clearing $1b are the offsets; the Tk24cr phantom-export fraud and the grid strain say the pressure is broadening, not lifting. The desk stays defensive on export-linked credit, positioned for the Q2 print and softening RMG receivables rather than the easy front.

metrics.sub: curated tape — RMG's EU slump and exporter energy stress lead
metrics.label: Headlines count

banker_read.verdict: The taka held 123.20 while gold eased to $4,380/oz from $4,431, the haven bid fading as Brent holds near $88.52. The buffer stays thin — reserves $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo against a $1.77bn trade gap the softening export line no longer comfortably clears. Steady, not safe.

tldr: Taka steady at 123.20; gold slips to $4,380 as the haven bid fades.
analysis: The taka's calm is real but shallow. USD/BDT held 123.20 even as the haven bid faded — gold eased to $4,380/oz from $4,431 — leaving the external account leaning on earned dollars that are thinning. That is the pressure point. RMG exports to the EU, the largest apparel market, fell 16.4% in H1, and exporters are seeking to spread July-August utility bills over twelve months; both point to a softer export line into a $1.77bn trade gap that a second sub-$3bn remittance month no longer comfortably clears. Reserves sat at $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo, and the August refresh is overdue — a figure below $36bn would confirm the drain the soft trade data imply. The desk position: respect 123.20 as a level, but treat the reserve refresh, not the daily spot, as the real test — the peg holds on a buffer no longer being topped up.

analysis: The macro read is one sentence stretched across eight prints: the money is there, the borrowers are not. Private credit growth sits at a 33-year-low 4.98% while M2 runs 10.52% on the Feb read — highest since Apr 2022 (10.9% then) — liquidity present, demand absent. The demand side is where today's news lands: RMG exporters, the largest hard-currency earners, are asking to spread July-August utility bills over twelve months as EU orders fall 16.4% in H1. Firms managing a cash-flow squeeze do not draw new working-capital lines. BB cut on 30 July, but the real policy rate is razor-thin at 0.34% on the Jun read and the CPI 12m-avg still prints 8.68% — highest since Dec 2025 (8.8% then). The desk read: hold before easing further — another cut buys liquidity the credit channel is not using.
